categories.name: T-Deck Plus · Conversation
categories.tagline: Make the keyboard and wired audio earn their place.

categories.name: T-Deck Plus · Away from Wi-Fi
categories.tagline: Use radio only when it is the right tool.

ideas.title: Keyboard-first shared chat
ideas.pitch: Compose and retry family turns with the Deck keys.
ideas.experience: A draft survives a weak link; Send never creates a second turn by accident.
ideas.how: Bind text editing to stable turn IDs and the shared authenticated HTTP route.
ideas.risks: Hardware key mapping and partial sends need physical tests.

ideas.title: Wired USB-C reply audio
ideas.pitch: Hear a completed reply through a powered wired headset.
ideas.experience: The Deck plays an approved voice clip with a visible stop control.
ideas.how: Finish the USB audio host path, verify clip identity and bound playback energy.
ideas.risks: ESP32-S3 USB host, power draw and accessory compatibility need bench tests.
ideas.audience: Families who prefer private wired audio

ideas.title: Clear USB recovery steps
ideas.pitch: Make a bad firmware day recoverable.
ideas.experience: A parent sees the exact Deck identity, backup and signed image before any write.
ideas.how: Build a device-aware recovery guide around existing TUF and backup receipts.
ideas.risks: Never erase user state or flash an unverified image.

ideas.title: Reply ledger for weak links
ideas.pitch: Make accepted, waiting and answered turns unmistakable on the Deck.
ideas.experience: A message typed on physical keys survives lost Wi-Fi and never duplicates after reconnect.
ideas.how: Pair the shared turn ID with a local outbox receipt and a compact status row on the 320×240 display.
ideas.risks: Flash wear, partial writes and reconnect order need physical soak tests.
ideas.audience: T-Deck users away from steady Wi-Fi

ideas.title: Physical-key quick actions
ideas.pitch: Make the keyboard useful even when the child is wearing gloves.
ideas.experience: One key opens Chat, one opens Scout Trail, and a visible shortcut sheet explains the rest.
ideas.how: Map hardware scan codes to shared Lua actions with long-press and repeat bounds.
ideas.risks: Hardware revisions and accidental sends need real keyboard testing.
ideas.audience: Kids who prefer the Deck keys

ideas.title: Store-and-forward radio turns
ideas.pitch: Queue a bounded message until a trusted internet peer can relay it.
ideas.experience: A field message waits locally, then reaches the same family thread once.
ideas.how: Use encrypted envelopes, explicit peer receipts, replay bounds and radio duty limits.
ideas.risks: US915 operation and real power use require hardware validation.

ideas.title: Keyboard-sized Lua apps
ideas.pitch: Give portable games real Deck controls.
ideas.experience: Scout Trail and future apps feel natural with keys, not a stretched watch canvas.
ideas.how: Map shared Lua actions to hardware keys and a readable 320×240 layout.
ideas.risks: App memory and key repeat need on-device testing.
ideas.audience: Kids using the Deck as a pocket computer

ideas.title: A Scout Trail field map
ideas.pitch: Give the Deck a small map that reacts to its shared Lua story.
ideas.experience: Choosing the creek path draws a readable route and an earned badge on the Deck screen.
ideas.how: Reuse Scout Trail state; add a Deck-specific canvas layout and keyboard focus.
ideas.risks: Screen memory and legibility in sunlight need hardware checks.

ideas.title: A short, explicit nearby game invite
ideas.pitch: Use the Deck radio only during a chosen local game.
ideas.experience: The child accepts a watch or tablet invite, plays one turn and sees the link go quiet.
ideas.how: Extend authenticated peer enrollment with separate app-session slots and bounded foreground messages.
ideas.risks: Current firmware has a single peer; battery cost and physical consent must be proven.
ideas.audience: Families with more than one Ackerman device
